confusing.title: The eight pairs students mix up in this chapter
rows: Equity: fluctuating dividend, full voting rights, paid last, costliest. Preference: fixed dividend, very limited voting rights, priority over equity, hybrid
Preference dividend is an appropriation and not tax-deductible. Debenture interest is a charge and is tax-deductible, so debt is cheaper
Callable: the issuer may redeem early at the call price. Puttable: the investor may sell the bond back before maturity
Drop lock bond vs convertible floating rate note
Drop lock: converts automatically from floating to fixed when the rate falls below a predetermined level. Convertible FRN: the holder chooses to convert into a longer-term debt security
Operating: short, cancellable, lessor bears maintenance and obsolescence, non-payout. Financial: long, non-cancellable, lessee bears them, full payout
Close-ended: the asset goes back to the lessor, who keeps the obsolescence and residual value risk. Open-ended: the lessee may purchase the asset at the end
Pre-shipment is packing credit for buying, manufacturing, processing, packing and shipping. Post-shipment bridges the gap until the proceeds arrive
Crowd funding is the broader concept; P2P lending is the category where lenders match with borrowers for unsecured loans through an online platform
P2P is a part, not an alternative
confusing.spot_it: Two questions settle almost every pair here: who holds the option, and who bears the loss if things go wrong.

cases.title: Integrated Case 1 — Meghna Exports Ltd. raises money on every front
facts: Meghna Exports Ltd. is setting up a new processing unit. A financial institution has sanctioned a ₹60 crore term loan, but disbursement will take four months. To avoid losing the building season, Meghna borrows ₹12 crore from its bank for that period, hypothecating movable assets and giving a demand promissory note; the rate is higher than the term-loan rate and the loan will be adjusted when the institution disburses.

For the equipment, Meghna does not buy outright. A leasing company purchases the machine, borrowing 80% of the cost from a bank, and leases it to Meghna. Meghna pays the rentals directly to that bank, and the surplus over the bank's dues goes to the leasing company, which claims the depreciation allowance.

Meghna has a confirmed export order backed by an irrevocable letter of credit. Its bank advances funds so that it can buy raw material, process, pack and ship the consignment; the advance must be squared off within 180 days by negotiating the export bills.

After shipment, the proceeds are still to be realised, so the bank discounts the usance export bills backed by bills of lading, and separately advances against duty drawback receivable on export performance — an advance of a clean nature.

To fund a green effluent-treatment plant, Meghna plans a bond whose proceeds are ring-fenced for that project, and its treasurer also suggests a bond whose proceeds would be free for general corporate purposes but tied to carbon-reduction targets.

questions.q: The ₹12 crore bank borrowing taken because the sanctioned term loan is not yet disbursed is:

options.C: Bridge finance

reasoning: SM §3.7: bridge finance refers to loans taken normally from commercial banks for a short period because of pending disbursement of loans sanctioned by financial institutions.
The facts match every feature: hypothecation of movable assets, a demand promissory note, a higher rate, and adjustment out of the term loan on disbursement.

questions.q: The equipment arrangement, in which a lender funds 80% of the cost and is repaid from the rentals directly by the user while the leasing company claims depreciation, is:

options.C: An open-ended lease

reasoning: SM §6.2: under a leveraged lease a third party is involved besides the lessor and lessee; the lessor borrows a part of the purchase cost (say 80%) from the lender, the asset is held as security, the lender is paid off from the lease rentals directly by the lessee, and the surplus goes to the lessor, who claims the depreciation allowance.
Three parties plus depreciation with the lessor identify it precisely.

questions.q: The advance taken against the irrevocable letter of credit to buy, process, pack and ship the goods is:

options.A: Packing credit, a form of pre-shipment finance
options.C: A deferred payment guarantee

reasoning: SM §7: pre-shipment finance generally takes the form of packing credit — an advance for buying, manufacturing, processing, packing and shipping goods to overseas buyers, available against a firm export order or an irrevocable letter of credit.
It must be liquidated within 180 days by negotiation of export bills or receipt of export proceeds.

questions.q: Discounting the usance export bills backed by bills of lading, and advancing against duty drawback receivable, are forms of:

options.C: Debt securitisation

reasoning: SM §7: post-shipment finance takes the forms of purchase or discounting of documentary export bills, ECGC guarantee, advance against export bills sent for collection, and advance against duty drawbacks and cash subsidy.
The study material calls advances against duty drawback 'of a clean nature', so the bank must exercise necessary precautions.

questions.q: The two bonds the treasurer is comparing are respectively:

options.A: A masala bond and a municipal bond
options.B: A drop lock bond and an option bond
options.C: A deep discount bond and a zero coupon bond
options.D: A project-based green bond and a target-based sustainability-linked bond

reasoning: SM §9: ESG bonds can be project-based — green bonds and social bonds — and target-based — sustainability-linked bonds.
Green bond proceeds finance 'green projects'; SLB proceeds are not meant for a specific project but for general corporate purposes to achieve Key Performance Indicators.

concepts: F02.22 pre- and post-shipment export finance
cases.trap: Every part here can be answered by naming the source. The mark is lost by describing the source without naming it, or by putting packing credit after shipment.

cases.title: Integrated Case 2 — Sarvodaya Finance Ltd. and a start-up it backs
facts: Sarvodaya Finance Ltd. has a large book of two-wheeler loans but no liquid secondary market for them. It sells the pool to a vehicle created for the purpose, which acts as a trustee for investors and issues coupon-bearing securities through merchant bankers to a pension fund. The arrangement is without recourse, and the borrowers keep paying their instalments as before.

Sarvodaya also runs a venture arm. It invests in Jalak Robotics, a start-up run by two technically qualified engineers, taking 42% of its equity and giving the founders help with sales strategy and business networking.
Part of the funding to Jalak is a loan on which no interest is charged, repayable as a royalty of 8% on sales once the venture generates revenue.

Jalak's founders also approach IDBI, which offers a facility that is interest free but carries a service charge of one per cent per annum for the first five years, with a repayment schedule fixed to the unit's repaying capacity and an initial moratorium.

To fund a product launch, Jalak raises small amounts from a large number of internet users, some in exchange for securities and some as loans matched on an online platform; a few contribute with no expectation of ownership or repayment at all.

questions.q: The vehicle that holds Sarvodaya's loan pool and issues securities against it is:

options.A: A Special Purpose Vehicle acting as trustee for investors
options.C: A primary dealer appointed by the RBI

reasoning: SM §5: in the pooling function, similar loans or receivables are clubbed to create an underlying pool of assets, and the pool is transferred in favour of the Special Purpose Vehicle, which acts as a trustee for investors.
The SPV then structures and issues securities, generally sold to investors through merchant bankers.

questions.q: Because the securitisation is 'without recourse', the credit risk is borne by:

options.B: The pension fund and other investors
options.C: The merchant bankers who sold the securities

reasoning: SM §5: the process is generally without recourse, i.e. investors bear the credit risk, and the issuer is under an obligation to pay investors only if the cash flows are received from the collateral.
The benefit to the originator is that assets are shifted off the balance sheet, giving it off-balance-sheet funding.

questions.q: Sarvodaya's 42% equity stake in Jalak, coupled with help on sales strategy and networking, illustrates:

options.B: Equity financing under venture capital, where the contribution does not exceed 49% so that control stays with the entrepreneur
options.C: A participating debenture

reasoning: SM §4.3: the equity contribution of the venture capital firm does not exceed 49% of the total equity capital, so that effective control and ownership remains with the entrepreneur.
SM §4.2: apart from providing funds, the investor also provides support in the form of sales strategy, business networking and management expertise.

questions.q: The interest-free loan repayable as a royalty on sales is:

options.C: A conditional loan

reasoning: SM §4.3: a conditional loan is repayable in the form of a royalty after the venture is able to generate sales, and no interest is paid on such loans; in India venture capital financiers charge royalty ranging between 2 and 15 per cent.
An income note would carry both interest and royalty, at substantially low rates.

questions.q: The IDBI facility and the internet-based fund raising are respectively:

options.B: Internal cash accruals and donation-based crowdfunding
options.C: A deferred payment guarantee and start-up funding
options.D: Seed capital assistance, and crowd funding comprising equity funding, P2P lending and donation

reasoning: SM §8: seed capital assistance is designed by IDBI for professionally or technically qualified entrepreneurs who lack adequate financial resources; it is interest free but carries a service charge of one per cent per annum for the first five years, with repayment fixed to repaying capacity and an initial moratorium of up to five years.
SM §10: crowdfunding collects funds in exchange for equity (equity funding), loans (P2P lending) or nothing at all (donation).

cases.trap: The 42% stake tempts students into 'control passes to the investor'. The study material's point is the opposite: the cap exists so that control stays with the entrepreneur.

mcqs.question: Funds required to finance permanent or hard-core working capital should, as per the study material, be procured from:

options.C: Advances from customers

mcqs.explanation: SM §1: long-term financial needs include funds for permanent or hard-core working capital.

mcqs.question: Preference share capital is described as a hybrid form of financing because:

options.A: It carries voting rights like equity and security like debt
options.B: Its dividend is fixed like interest, but like equity dividend it is not a tax-deductible payment
options.C: It is redeemable like debentures and perpetual like equity at the same time
options.D: It can be issued only along with debentures

mcqs.explanation: SM §3.2: it resembles equity because preference dividend, like equity dividend, is not tax-deductible, and debt because the rate of dividend is fixed.

mcqs.question: A fully convertible debenture generally carries an interest rate that is:

options.A: Higher than on a non-convertible debenture, to compensate for conversion
options.B: Equal to the preference dividend rate
options.C: Lower than on a non-convertible debenture, because of the attraction of conversion into equity

mcqs.explanation: SM §3.4: interest rates on fully convertible debentures are generally lower than on non-convertible debentures because of the conversion attraction.

mcqs.question: A rupee-denominated bond that Indian corporate borrowers sell to investors in overseas markets is called a:

options.C: Samurai bond

mcqs.explanation: SM §3.5: masala bond is the Indian name for a rupee-denominated bond sold by Indian borrowers to investors in overseas markets.

mcqs.question: Under a participating debenture used in venture capital financing, interest is:

options.A: Not charged in the start-up phase, charged at a low rate up to a particular level of operation, and at a high rate thereafter
options.B: Charged at a flat rate throughout
options.C: Replaced entirely by a royalty on sales
options.D: Payable only on maturity along with a redemption premium

mcqs.explanation: SM §4.3: a participating debenture carries charges in three phases.

mcqs.question: In the securitisation function, the securities issued by the SPV are generally sold to investors through:

options.C: The original borrowers

mcqs.explanation: SM §5: the securities are generally sold to investors through merchant bankers; investors are pension funds, mutual funds and insurance funds.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes an operating lease?

options.A: It is non-cancellable and runs for the full economic life of the asset
options.B: The lessee bears the risk of obsolescence
options.C: It is usually full payout
options.D: The lease is kept cancellable by the lessor, who can lease the same asset to other willing lessees

mcqs.explanation: SM §6.1: as the lessor has no difficulty in leasing the same asset to another willing lessee, the lease is kept cancellable by the lessor; it is usually non-payout.

mcqs.question: In a sales-aid lease, the lessor earns from:

options.C: Both the lessee and the manufacturer, who may grant credit or a commission
options.D: A third-party lender who funds the purchase

mcqs.explanation: SM §6.2: in consideration of the aid in sales the manufacturer may grant either credit or a commission, so the lessor earns from both sources.

mcqs.question: A company can accept public deposits up to a maximum of:

options.A: 35 per cent of its paid-up capital and reserves
options.C: 49 per cent of its equity capital
options.D: 80 per cent of its fixed assets

mcqs.explanation: SM §7: public deposits may be accepted subject to RBI stipulations up to a maximum of 35 per cent of paid-up capital and reserves, for six months to three years.

mcqs.question: Unsecured loans given by promoters to meet the promoters' contribution norm carry interest that:

options.A: Must exceed the rate on institutional loans
options.C: Should be less than or equal to the rate of interest on institutional loans, and is payable only after institutional dues
options.D: Is fixed by the Reserve Bank of India

mcqs.explanation: SM §8: the rate should be less than or equal to the institutional rate and interest can be paid only after payment of institutional dues.

mcqs.question: External Commercial Borrowings are commercial loans availed from non-resident lenders with a minimum average maturity of:

options.C: 1 year

mcqs.explanation: SM §9: ECBs are availed from non-resident lenders with a minimum average maturity of 3 years, under the Automatic or Approval route.

mcqs.question: A foreign currency option, as distinguished from a foreign currency future, is:

options.A: An obligation to buy or sell a specified currency for settlement at a future date
options.B: The right, and not the obligation, to buy or sell foreign currency at a specified price on or before a specified date
options.C: A floating rate note issued up to seven years maturity
options.D: A short-term money market instrument denominated in US dollars

mcqs.explanation: SM §9: an FC option is a right and not an obligation; FC futures are obligations and not rights.

descriptive.question: Explain any four types of lease other than the operating lease and the financial lease.
answer_points: **Sale and lease back:** the owner sells the asset to a buyer who leases it back to him for lease rentals; the asset is not physically exchanged and it all happens in records only. The seller assumes the role of lessee and the buyer the role of lessor; the seller gets the agreed selling price and the buyer gets the lease rentals.

**Leveraged lease:** a third party is involved besides the lessor and the lessee. The lessor borrows part of the purchase cost (say 80%) from the lender, the asset is held as security, the lender is paid from the lease rentals directly by the lessee, the surplus goes to the lessor, and the lessor claims depreciation allowance.

**Sales-aid lease:** the lessor ties up with a manufacturer to market the latter's product through his own leasing operations; in consideration the manufacturer may grant credit or a commission, so the lessor earns from both the lessee and the manufacturer.

**Close-ended and open-ended leases:** in a close-ended lease the assets get transferred to the lessor at the end and the risk of obsolescence and residual value remains with the lessor as legal owner; in an open-ended lease the lessee has the option of purchasing the asset at the end of the lease period.

descriptive.question: Explain the methods of venture capital financing.
answer_points: **Equity financing:** venture capital finance is generally provided by way of equity share capital, because the undertaking needs funds for a longer period and may not be able to provide returns in the initial stages. The venture capital firm's equity contribution does not exceed 49% of total equity capital, so effective control and ownership remains with the entrepreneur.

**Conditional loan:** repayable as a royalty after the venture generates sales, with no interest paid; in India the royalty ranges between 2 and 15 per cent, the rate depending on gestation period, cash flow patterns and risk. Some financiers offer the choice of a high rate of interest, well above 20 per cent, instead of royalty once the venture becomes commercially sound.

**Income note:** a hybrid security combining conventional and conditional loan features; the entrepreneur pays both interest and royalty on sales but at substantially low rates. IDBI's VCF provides funding equal to 80–87.50% of project cost for commercial application of indigenous technology.
**Participating debenture:** charges in three phases — no interest in the start-up phase, a low rate up to a particular level of operation, and a high rate thereafter.

descriptive.question: What are the key features of bridge financing, and how does it differ from an ordinary bank overdraft?
answer_points: Bridge finance refers to loans taken by a company normally from commercial banks for a short period because of pending disbursement of loans sanctioned by financial institutions.
The bridge loans are repaid or adjusted out of the term loans as and when disbursed by the concerned institutions.
They are normally secured by hypothecating movable assets, personal guarantees and demand promissory notes.
Generally the rate of interest on bridge finance is higher as compared with that on term loans.

An overdraft, by contrast, lets a customer withdraw in excess of the credit balance in the current account up to a fixed limit, is repayable on demand but generally continues by annual renewal, and carries interest on daily balances; it is not linked to any sanctioned term loan.

descriptive.question: Explain debt securitisation and state the benefit it gives to the originator.
answer_points: Securitisation is a process in which illiquid assets are pooled into marketable securities that can be sold to investors, creating instruments that represent ownership interest in, or are secured by, a segregated income-producing asset or pool of assets.
**Origination function:** a borrower seeks a loan from a finance company or bank; creditworthiness is evaluated and a contract entered into with a repayment schedule over the life of the loan.
**Pooling function:** similar loans or receivables are clubbed together into an underlying pool; the pool is transferred in favour of a Special Purpose Vehicle, which acts as a trustee for investors.

**Securitisation function:** the SPV structures and issues securities against the asset pool, carrying a coupon and expected maturity, asset-based or mortgage-based, generally sold through merchant bankers to pension funds, mutual funds and insurance funds.

The process is generally without recourse, so investors bear the credit risk and the issuer pays only if the cash flows are received from the collateral. The benefit to the originator is that assets are shifted off the balance sheet, giving it recourse to off-balance-sheet funding, and it is a method of recycling funds to support further lending.

descriptive.question: An exporter has shipped goods but the proceeds are not yet realised. Identify the type of finance he should seek and explain any three of its forms.
answer_points: The finance required is **post-shipment finance**, provided by commercial banks after shipment of goods.

**Purchase or discounting of documentary export bills:** finance by purchasing export bills drawn payable at sight or discounting usance export bills covering confirmed sales, backed by documents of title such as a bill of lading, post parcel receipts or air consignment notes.

**E.C.G.C. guarantee:** post-shipment finance through purchase, negotiation or discount of an export bill against an order qualifies for the post-shipment export credit guarantee, provided the exporter obtains a shipment or contracts risk policy covering political and commercial risks; the Corporation fixes credit limits for individual exporters.

**Advance against export bills sent for collection:** banks advance against export bills forwarded through them for collection, considering the creditworthiness of the party, nature of goods exported, usance and standing of the drawee.

**Advance against duty drawbacks and cash subsidy:** banks advance against duty drawback and cash subsidy receivable against export performance; such advances are of a clean nature, so precautions are necessary. Such an advance must be liquidated within 180 days from the date of shipment.

descriptive.question: Explain Environmental, Social and Governance linked bonds, and distinguish crowd funding from Peer-to-Peer lending.
answer_points: ESG bonds carry a responsibility of the issuer company to prioritise optimal environmental, social and governance factors; investing in them is considered socially responsible investing. They can be project-based — green bonds and social bonds — and target-based — sustainability-linked bonds.

Green bonds are issued by a financial, non-financial or public institution and the proceeds finance 'green projects' aimed at positive environmental or climate impact; social bonds finance socially impactful projects relating to human rights, equality and animal welfare; sustainability-linked bonds combine both, with proceeds used for general corporate purposes to achieve Key Performance Indicators.

Crowd funding means raising money for an individual or organisation from a group of people to fund a project, typically via the internet, in exchange for equity, loans or nothing at all; three parties are involved — the fund raiser, the mediator and the fund investor.

P2P lending is that category of crowdfunding where lenders match with borrowers to provide unsecured loans through an online platform; the funds are repaid with interest, though the lending involves a risk of default.
Hence crowd funding is the broader concept and P2P lending is basically a part of crowd funding.

quick.a: Based on basic sources, on maturity of payment, and on ownership and control.

differentiate.a: Callable: the issuer has the right to redeem before maturity at the call price. Puttable: the investor has the right to sell the bond back to the company before maturity.
Financial: long, non-cancellable, lessee bears maintenance and obsolescence, full payout. Operating: short, cancellable by the lessor, lessor bears maintenance and obsolescence, non-payout.
Conditional loan: royalty on sales, no interest. Income note: both interest and royalty, at substantially low rates.

Pre-shipment is packing credit for buying, manufacturing, processing, packing and shipping. Post-shipment covers bills purchased or discounted, ECGC guarantee, advances against bills for collection and against duty drawback.
ADRs and GDRs let an Indian company raise foreign capital abroad. IDRs let a foreign company raise funds from the Indian capital market, listed and traded in India.
Equity funding gives the investor securities and a stake in the organisation. Donation-based crowdfunding carries no expectation of any ownership or debt.
